findings.text: the map says the lane-change miss affects 5 of the 13 census runs; measured on the population it names, exactly 4 carry a lane-change stream (r-20260925T090349791305 with lane-change-3.jsonl; r-20260925T124323355400, r-20260926T104635341057 and r-20260926T105233192444 with lane-change-2.jsonl) and those same 4 are exactly the runs whose full stream set exceeds the production reader's candidate set (stream.jsonl plus resume-*.jsonl). The count is one too high. The defect under it is real and larger than stated: in all four the production fold reads only claude-dialect streams while the rollout it is priced against is codex, so the miss is most of the run's spend, not a slice — measured, r-20260925T124323355400 folds to 150,433 charged tokens against a 30,310,691 rollout.

the counter-example's explanation does not hold up: it reads the 100.6% sum as evidence that 'summing is right' where the streams are a different thread. Decomposed, the codex lane-change-2.jsonl alone is 30,333,105 charged = 100.07% of the 30,310,691 rollout, and the claude stream.jsonl contributes 150,433 tokens (0.5%) on top for the census's 100.6%. The ratio is a small cross-provider addend, not a demonstration that the fold is right, and the rule a builder takes from this trap — add the lane-change stream to the same run total — would add one provider's tokens into another's, which the per-budget-group figure of §1 cannot carry. The correct rule (a lane-change stream is counted in its own thread and its own budget group) is not stated.

'Five of the 13 codex runs above ... and drop out of the census for exactly this reason' is contradicted by the census the map ships: that script globs all *.jsonl, so the lane-change runs are inside its 13 rows and appear in its own table at 100.6%, 129.4%, 133.3% and 160.7%. What the production reader drops is a different set question from what the census includes — the distinction the section exists to draw.

DETAIL_FIELDS is cited twice as 'line 27'; the declaration is at reckon/run_store.py:32 (line 27 is a line of the comment block documenting it). Minor, and invisible to the node's own citation gate because it is written as a bare 'line 27' rather than a path:line the resolver matches.

the two instruments are advertised as re-runnable by a later reader, but neither runs under the host's default python3 — measured, python3 is 3.11.5 and both die with SyntaxError at reckon/crew/quota_weight.py:212 (a 3.12 type statement) before reading anything — and neither script nor either log records the interpreter, the revision, the tree or the cwd it ran from. Under the project interpreter (~/Code/reckon/.venv/bin/python, 3.14.2) both reproduce the recorded figures exactly.

item_verdicts.goal: §4's four deliverables each carry a row: (1) preflight runway and refusal, (2) resumed burn as cumulative minus the previous attempt's last cumulative, (3) dispatch writing the backend into the run store, (4) per-lane-and-day share of dispatches that continued another task's session. Every file the done-when names is cited — budget.py (30 refs), crew/rollout.py, crew/quota_weight.py:215, crew/runs.py (pointer_path():73), crew/dispatch.py (1184/1228/7681), velocity.py (140/460/587/948/1333) — each row states present vs missing and names the second implementation to reuse, the node split keeps every node off dispatch.py, promotion.py and cli.py and says node E waits on the peers holding them, and the fixture is stated with host run directories that all exist.
item_verdicts.instruments: my re-run of both scripts reproduces the recorded output row for row: census 13 runs, 12 with a locatable rollout, ratios [100.6, 115.5, 129.4, 133.3, 149.4, 154.6, 160.6, 160.7, 166.5, 175.1, 181.0, 227.1] (median 157.6); newest-attempt probe 8 of 8 within 0.03–0.10%, sum 0 of 8 within 1%. item_verdicts.manifest: read; the read sha (af15a34b), both instrument logs and the four deliverable rows are named; baseline_suite and after_suite are the contract's JSON with completed:false and an explicit reason — the reviewed run edits no repository file, so neither arm is absent evidence masquerading as a measured zero. The manifest's record commit field is empty for the same structural reason its own follow_ons item 4 names.
item_verdicts.store_fix: the recommended one-entry fix is real, verified by reading and by query: QUERY_KEYS drives schema, indexes, insert and migration from one declaration, and _migrate_runs' backfill path runs on every open of the live store because its eleven legacy columns never equal the six-column _RUNS_COLUMNS — _legacy_payload returns the stored payload blob, so a 'backend' entry in QUERY_KEYS would be filled from it on the next open, repairing history rather than only new rows. My own read of the live table: 22 non-null backend of 6225 rows, all dated 2026-09-09/10, payload carrying a non-empty backend on 6199 — the map's 6201/6223 and 6197/6223, both grown by the store's own growth.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared report path is the only artifact outside the run directory; the reviewed repository worktree is clean at a5a906af with no commit and no tracked edit, and the four helper scripts sit inside the run directory the HOST line names. Nothing the map proposes writes a peer-held file.

justifications.durability: the map pins its read sha and every cited file except recovery.py is unchanged from its own base to that sha; the recovery.py anchors are five references that shift by three lines at the tip, mitigated by the header's read-sha instruction; the instruments reproduce but not under the host's default interpreter, and neither names its interpreter or revision, so a later reader must supply both.
justifications.evidence: reproducibility is the map's strongest property — both instruments re-run to identical figures on my own invocation, the anchor set resolves and names what it claims, the headline done-when measurement (3 resumed codex streams priced within 1% rather than at 157%) is supported by 8 of 8 within 0.10% against 0 of 8 for the sum, the absence claim for the runs denominator carries a positive control that reproduces (0 run-ish matches across three modules; remaining=14 in budget.py, all window arithmetic), and the store census and the one-entry fix both verify. Deducted for the off-by-one count, the mis-decomposed counter-example, and the census range being presented as resume overcount when 4 of its 12 priced rows are cross-provider sums.
justifications.fit: report-only node, markdown at the path its fence fixes; mechanism names only, no plan or ticket identifiers, no version suffixes, no second implementation proposed anywhere — each row names the single existing owner to extend, and the split works along seams the code already declares (budget_group.declared_groups, pace.drain_deadline, velocity.lane). The one point held back is the DETAIL_FIELDS pointer landing five lines above its declaration.
justifications.goal_fidelity: every element the fence asks for is present and checkable, and the four rows land on the right seams; the deduction is §2's trap narrative, the passage that steers the build node most directly, carrying two factual slips (the affected-run count and the counter-example's decomposition) and one rule that is wrong as written for a quota measure.
justifications.scope_discipline: one write path, honoured exactly; the repository is untouched and no commit exists; no peer-held file is written or proposed to be written; the map reads freely and returns outcome data only.
